name: IPSI Spatial Glass

units.px: px on the 1080x1920 render canvas (= 720x1280 reference measurement x1.5)
units.px720: keys ending in 720 hold the raw reference measurement in 720x1280 px
units.pct: keys ending in Pct are % of canvas width (x) or height (y); identical at 720 and 1080
units.frames: keys ending in F (durationF, startOffsetF, tF ...) are frames at 30 fps, the render rate
units.colour: #RRGGBB (uppercase) or rgba(); gradients are CSS strings
units.keyframes: list of objects with tMs (optional tF) plus the animated property name
units.gainDb: dB relative to full scale for the engine mixer (audio.py)
units.layers: engine layer names: bg | behind | front | fx (plateWrap / talentWrap for the camera targets)
units.note: All px values are for the 1080x1920 canvas (= reference px x 1.5). *720 fields give the reference value. xPct/yPct are % of canvas width/height and identical at both resolutions. Durations: ms at 30 fps (1 frame = 33.3 ms); *F fields give frames.

fonts.note: Original letterforms are about 1.46x wider than Readex Pro at equal height (SF Arabic suspected). Size by ink height, widen with scaleX up to 1.3, then add kashida. The Readex HEXP axis was tested and rejected: it letter-spaces the word instead of widening the glyphs.
Calibrated: Readex 700 at 123 px@720 reproduces the وبسبب ink box 395x88 px exactly. Flat white, no effects.

effects.glowNote: Revised after a render vs k_020: the halo is wide and grey-white (row y=200@720: #1A2C43 -> #505C6D), with only a thin saturated cyan edge. The earlier rgba(121,181,244,.55) r60 x1.2 rendered as a saturated neon-sign glow.

neonRim.sides: top/left outer contours + the lower inner edges of the counters (k_020 zoom); built as a filled copy shifted up-left under the face, above the extrusion

fauxBold.note: Readex Pro stops at 700; the reference is 800-900. Add a same-tone 4 px stroke.

fill.note: Opacity gradients are static. The left and right alefs fade in opposite directions. The talent's arms show through the glyphs.

fonts.note: Monoline. Readex, IBM Plex and Noto at weight 200 are indistinguishable at this size. Long kashida is drawn as a glowing line.

bevel.implementation: filter: drop-shadow(0 -1px 0 highlight) drop-shadow(0 2px 2px shadow) on the wrapper. text-shadow would show through the transparent fill.

fonts.note: Original is probably SF Pro Display Bold, about 10% wider than Inter. Size by cap/x-height, then open the tracking.

tatweel.insertAfter: first joining letter: ه ف ك ط م ع ح

grade.intent: Low-key teal/orange. Plate highlights roll off near luma 165-170, so graphics own the only true whites. Shadows are crushed to near-black with a faint blue/magenta bias. Mids are teal, skin stays warm, saturation is high.

ffmpeg.normalize: eq=gamma=G:brightness=B  -> choose G (1.0-1.5) so the face-box median luma before the look curve is about 0.50 (128)
ffmpeg.bottomFade: geq or overlay: linear black gradient from 0% at y=62%H to 55% opacity at y=100%H
ffmpeg.tested: On ref1/ref3 frames: p0.5=0, p95=120-129, p99.9=161-164. These hit the targets. Warm sets stay warm, so the teal must come from the set, the background replacement or the lighting.

glowBloomOnPractical.note: Only plate practicals (ceiling tubes) bloom. Do not add global bloom.

wsPlate.use: WS when the source set is warm, bright or busy (bg-replace with the person matte)
wsPlate.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of an empty modern [clinic / studio / lab / office matching the topic] at night, low-key cinematic lighting, dark teal and cyan painted walls, two cyan-white fluorescent tube fixtures on the ceiling at upper left and upper right with soft haze, blue LED under-glow on equipment at the right side, a dark grey counter softly out of focus in the left foreground, empty space at centre for a seated person, 35 mm lens f/4, crushed blacks, saturated teal, no people, no text, no logos.
wsPlate.negativePrompt: warm light, orange or beige walls, daylight, windows, people, text.
wsPlate.motion: locked off (no drift): the punch-in pull-back reads as a camera move only on a static plate

mcuPlate.prompt: 9:16 extreme shallow depth-of-field background plate of a dark clinic interior, everything defocused into large smooth bokeh, deep dark teal on the left (#162D4B), saturated blue-cyan glow on the right (#00367D), one soft pale blurred lamp shape at upper centre-right, no recognisable objects, no people, no text.

tubeHaze.note: one around each ceiling tube; no particles

cyanRimRelight.note: relight the talent towards the plate; darken the bottom with overlays.bottomFade

darkCoolSet.use: source set already dark, cool or neutral: grade (grade.ffmpeg) and add cyan practicals (bloom blobs at the top corners)

worldLockSpec.what: Text/UI whose preset or component has worldLock:true receives the same transform as the plate during pullback-two-step (same origin, same scale keys), so it shrinks and drops with the camera.
worldLockSpec.formula1080: x = ox + (xFinal - ox) * S, y = oy + (yFinal - oy) * S, scale = S, with (ox, oy) = focusPx (540, 787) and S = current camera scale / final camera scale
worldLockSpec.measuredFit: hero height 243 -> 187 px (@720) in step 2 while the camera ratio is 0.795
worldLockSpec.runtimeNote: the engine scales only #plateWrap and #talentWrap; wrap world-locked cues in a container driven by the camera tween

textPresets.note: Becomes green/navy/brown where props or bright lights pass behind it. No mask animation. The Difference blend does it.

cameraMoves.trigger: Hard cut into a key-message WS. Used on 3 of 5 WS: hook, feature and CTA set-up.
cameraMoves.matchCut: Choose scaleFrom so the WS face width is about 0.8x the previous MCU face (reference: MCU face 210 px, punched-in WS face 165 px @720).
cameraMoves.sourceResolution: Needs a 4K source (vertical crop >= 1215x2160). At 2.49x a 1080p source upscales to soft mush. The reference hides softness with motion blur.

cameraMoves.trigger: Engine variant for footage that has no wide shot (CU/MCU plates such as renders/plates/doctor). Same timing, near-hold and fitted curves as pullback-two-step, with the scale keys compressed in log space (S_mcu = S_ref^0.5), so the punched-in face is ~1.6x the rest framing instead of ~2.5x. Rendered on the doctor plate: S_ref 2.49 would put the CU face at ~115% W on a 720p-sourced plate.
engine split of pullback-two-step: cue at shot start
engine split of pullback-two-step: cue at shot start + 1200 ms (36 F)
All other shots: static WS (turn and proof beats) and every MCU/CU
cameraMoves.note: No punch-ins, no drift, no shake. Rotation stays under 0.6 deg.

params.placement: in a speech pause; next phrase starts 1-3 F (33-100 ms) after the cut

params.sizes: MCU face 210 px <-> WS face 66 px @720 (3.2x)

params.rule: Graphics never animate out. The whole graphic layer ends with its shot.

pacing.endNote: hard-cut end on the spoken CTA (clean MCU, 3.37 s); no card, logo, hold or fade

cadence.why: The reference shows a 2-2-1 judder (50 fps master decimated to 30). Render natively at 30 fps for a smoother but non-identical feel.

music.character: none: dialogue-led mix (speech RMS p50 -17.8 dBFS)
music.note: No music bed detected. Dialogue-led. Room tone about -30 dBFS (50 Hz hum) is incidental; do not add.

sfxPolicy: Sparse, tonal SFX tied to a graphic type (gold shimmer, glass chime, near-inaudible ticks on type-ons). No whoosh, impact or riser on cuts or pull-backs. No music bed.

shimmerTwoTone.recipeNote: engine audio.py recipe: flat 9250 Hz 100 ms (+30 ms release) then 5600 Hz 60 ms at -4 dB, overlapping the release

tick8k1Series.recipeNote: engine audio.py recipe: five 8.1 kHz ticks (2 ms attack, 20 ms decay) plus the measured 4 kHz blip (140 ms, -2 dB) at +400 ms

sfx.offsetNote: the gold cue starts at the 3 F pre-glow, so +100 ms lands the shimmer on the centre glyph body
sfx.measured: 9252 Hz 5.17-5.27 s, 5597 Hz 5.27-5.33 s; reused at 29.55 s. Band level -32..-41 dBFS vs speech about -12 dBFS. Lands on the first glyph (S3) or on the outer glyphs (S9, +200 ms).
8.1 kHz ticks 6.18-6.46 / 6.75-6.85 s plus a 4.0 kHz event 6.58-6.72 s; band level about -57 dBFS (barely audible)
7.21 kHz at 30.72-31.03 and 31.20 s, about -48 dBFS; one per word
11.40-11.88 s, the loudest SFX: 4.09 kHz partial about -25 dBFS. Starts 1 F before the cut into the UI shot.

sfx.condition: only when the shot carries visionos-glass-ui

safe.note: marginPct/marginPx = distance from each edge; boxPx = safe rectangle corners on the 1080x1920 canvas

director.note: srt2scene only drafts. Assign per-shot hero materials, components and the pull-back by hand using the narrative template in STYLE.md. Defaults changed after the engine renders: neon-thin-blurfade's default position (63.2%, 22%) is the hook's WS slot and landed on the forehead on MCU footage (demo/scene_test.json still 75), so drafted captions now use neon-thin-typeon on the chest band (49.6%, 76%), which is also the reference's problem-beat pairing (hero-white-rise top + typed neon line on the chest). Its 3 x 8 kashida joints make 4-word lines overflow the 938 px safe width, hence 3 words. No punch-ins: the style is locked off except for hand-placed pull-backs (pullback-two-step, or pullback-two-step-mcu on CU/MCU-only footage).

do: One Arabic hero word per graphic shot at 55-86% frame width; every hero gets a different material (difference-peach, flat white, cyan glass + neon rim, gold light panel, gold spotlight)
Reprise the gold light-panel + glass pill template (same position, same shimmer SFX) for the CTA set-up
Pair each hero with a weaker English literal translation (ghost centre-hot, script hairline or peach accent) that overlaps or butts against it
Put heroes in the top band, behind the head when it overlaps (roto). Put support lines and glass UI over the chest band, in front
Alternate WS and MCU on hard cuts in speech pauses; open key-message WS shots with pullback-two-step and parent their text to the camera
Leave about 36% of runtime as clean talking head (later MCUs), including one tighter CU
Use kashida, not tracking, to widen Arabic. Thin captions turn long kashida into glowing lines
Keep holds perfectly static; only 3D props, carousels and phone screens loop
Grade low-key teal with crushed blacks and highlight roll-off near luma 168 so graphics own the whites
Keep SFX tonal, sparse and tied to a graphic type (shimmer for gold, chime for glass UI, quiet ticks for type-on)
dont: Don't set a full sentence large or put two heroes in one shot
Don't animate anything out; the cut removes it
Don't cover the face, or place text in the bottom 12.5% or top 5.5%
Don't use whooshes, impacts, risers, flashes, whip pans, shakes or music beat-sync
Don't add glow-breathing, slow push-ins or drift during holds
Don't put graphics on every shot. Later MCUs stay clean
Don't end on a CTA card, logo or fade; end on the spoken CTA with a hard cut
Don't use Readex weights above 700 (they don't exist); fake extra weight with a same-tone stroke
Don't grade a warm set toward teal and expect the look; replace or relight the background

residualUncertainty: Original fonts are unconfirmed (likely SF Arabic / SF Pro; Readex Pro and Inter are the closest installed matches). The script font is a Pinyon Script guess.
visionOS window 3D rotation values are estimates (bottom edge reads as a diagonal); the other UI sizes were measured at frame 420 only.
3D prop yaw speeds are visual estimates (30-60 deg/s).
SFX gains are derived from narrow-band levels, not broadband loudness; audition them.
The cyan glass extrusion offset and depth are construction guesses that match the look (rim colour, gradients and glow were measured).
